**(B)** pancreas

The exocrine part of the pancreas is made of acini, and the acinar cells secrete the alkaline pancreatic juice with its digestive enzymes. The liver is built of hepatic cells in lobules, gastric glands have mucus, chief and parietal cells, and the intestinal glands are the crypts of Lieberkuhn.

**(D)** Molars

Each half of each jaw has 2 incisors, 1 canine, 2 premolars and 3 molars. Multiplying by four half-jaws gives 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars and 12 molars in an adult, so molars are the most numerous.

**(C)** Talking

Tasting food, mixing saliva into it and pushing the bolus into the pharynx during swallowing are all parts of digestion in the buccal cavity. Talking is a function of the tongue too, but it has nothing to do with digestion, so it is the odd one out.

**(D)** Protease

Ptyalin is the name of salivary amylase, so the pair names an enzyme and the class it belongs to. Pepsin digests proteins into peptones and proteoses, so its class is protease. Lipase digests fats, galactose is a sugar, and the proenzyme is pepsinogen, the inactive form of pepsin, not its class.

[Note: the chapter does not state this; standard biology gives ptyalin as the other name of salivary amylase.]
